No shortcut uses Ctrl+Alt on Windows or Linux (#95).

Windows treats AltGr as Ctrl+Alt. A German layout types ``[``, ``]``, ``{``,
``}``, ``@``, ``\`` and ``€`` with AltGr, so a Ctrl+Alt shortcut would fire
while someone types. Ctrl+Alt is ⌘⌥ on macOS, which has no AltGr.

Press ``key`` with Ctrl+Alt, as Windows reports an AltGr press.

    qtbot.keyClick goes through Qt's shortcut matching before the widget
    sees the key. A one-character str also sets that character as the text.
macOS has no AltGr; ⌥⌘[ and ⌥⌘] are Fold and Unfold

Time large JSON documents and check the format size gates.

The 1 MB and 2 MB fixtures are built in memory from ``random.Random`` with a
fixed seed: nested objects and arrays, long strings, and non-ASCII text.
Nothing large is written into the tree. Timings are printed as one table.
They are not a pass/fail gate. One sample from each CI runner is not a
median, and a shared runner is too noisy to fail the job on raw seconds.

Parse and format go through ``format_json``. Collapse is the editor's
Collapse all (#64), with folding turned on as it is for Output; the fold
scan runs before the clock starts, as the Format worker runs it. Search uses
the editor's find on a marker planted at the end of the fixture. Syntax
coloring is the editor highlighter turning on for that document. Change
markers use the gutter API from the Compare prep work. The diff engine is
timed only when ``galley.core.diff.diff`` is importable; this checkout does
not invent one.

The hard checks are the JSON busy spinner, the progress bar, and the size
warning. Those follow ``JSON_BUSY_BYTES``, ``JSON_PROGRESS_BYTES``, and
``JSON_WARNING_BYTES``.

A second table times the same content on one line: 1.6 MB of compact JSON
in a single block, the shape that stalled the editor (#91). It records
setText and a keystroke with Show Whitespace and colors wanted and with
both off. The long-line guard in ``editor.py`` keeps the two close; the
hard budget for that keystroke lives in ``test_long_line_guard.py``.

Return ``count`` items from ``seed``.

    The generator is reseeded on every call, so item ``i`` does not depend on
    how many items a binary search asked for earlier.

Return pretty-printed JSON of exactly ``target`` UTF-8 bytes.

    The item count is a binary search, so generation does not re-dump the
    document once per item. The pad is ASCII, so each extra character is one
    UTF-8 byte.

Return compact JSON of exactly ``target`` UTF-8 bytes on one line.

    The same items as ``_build``, without indentation. The pad is ASCII.

Return formatted text, parse seconds, and the rest of ``format_json``.

    Parse runs from the start of the call through ``json.loads``, including
    the checks in front of the parser. Format is the rest of the call.

Return ``(diff, load_document)``, or None when Compare has no engine yet.

    ``diff`` compares two documents that ``load_document`` parsed and located.

Very long lines switch off whitespace dots and colors until they go (#91).

QPlainTextEdit lays out a whole block on every edit to it. On a one-line
1.6 MB JSON document, Show Whitespace made a keystroke take 10 s and the
highlighter added up to half a second more. The editor keeps the user's
choices and applies them only while every line is under the gates in
``editor.py``. Fixtures are built in memory: nothing large is in the tree.
One giant line: no dots, highlighter detached, View action still checked.
1.6 MB on one line, both options wanted: a keystroke takes under 3 s.

Cancel, format, and cancel again while the first worker is still alive.

    Both cancels stay inside the reap deadline. A second job must not start
    another replacement, queue a stuck worker twice, or replace the
    Cancelled status with the crash banner.

Cancel the replacement after the first child's reap deadline.

    Both children stay stuck. Each temp stays queued once, and neither
    file is deleted until its own child exits or the window shuts down.
    The poll and shutdown do not join. After the second Cancel the window
    shows the previous result, with Format enabled and no crash banner.

Format right after a second cancel does not announce an earlier reap.

    The first worker is already past ``REAP_DEADLINE_MS``. The second has
    just been cancelled. Format then runs on the replacement. The user did
    not wait on a worker that died, so the crash banner stays hidden.

Structural diff of two JSON or YAML documents (#65 PR 1).

Objects match by key and ignore key order. Arrays match by index. Scalars
compare by type and value. A unique identical subtree under a different
parent is Moved. Changes come in left-document order with spans into
each side's text.

Property checks for the structural diff (#65 PR 1).

The generators stay small (few leaves, a three-letter key alphabet) so
the two sides share keys often and the suite stays fast on Windows CI.
Equality under the diff's value rules: 1 == 1.0, true != 1, NaN == NaN.

Rebuild the right document from the left one and ``changes``.

    A Change carries summaries, which are cut at 80 characters, so the new
    values of Added, Changed, and Moved are read from ``right`` at their
    right path. That lookup is test-only. Everything else comes from the
    changes: which left values go (Removed, the source of a Moved), which
    are replaced (Changed), and where right-only values go in each parent
    (Added, the target of a Moved). Kept array items keep their order, so
    they fill the right indexes no insertion takes.

Time ``format_json`` with and without the duplicate check on ~2 MB.

    The printed numbers go in the PR. The bound is loose on purpose: the
    check may cost at most half again the format time, which only a per-key
    scan on the valid path would break. Runs alternate so both share noise.

import sys

from galley.core.format import format_json, format_yaml


def line_column(exc):
    lineno = getattr(exc, "lineno", None)
    colno = getattr(exc, "colno", None)
    if isinstance(lineno, int) and isinstance(colno, int):
        return lineno, colno
    mark = getattr(exc, "problem_mark", None)
    if (
        mark is not None
        and isinstance(getattr(mark, "line", None), int)
        and isinstance(getattr(mark, "column", None), int)
    ):
        return mark.line + 1, mark.column + 1
    return None


kind = sys.argv[1]
depth = sys.getrecursionlimit() + 100
if kind == "json":
    text = "[" * depth + "0" + "]" * depth
    format_text = format_json
else:
    lines = [f"{'  ' * level}k:" for level in range(depth)]
    lines.append(f"{'  ' * depth}1")
    text = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    format_text = format_yaml
try:
    format_text(text)
except RecursionError:
    raise SystemExit(2)
except Exception as exc:
    located = line_column(exc)
    if located is None:
        raise SystemExit(3)
    line, column = located
    if line < 1 or column < 1:
        raise SystemExit(3)
    raise SystemExit(0)
raise SystemExit(4)

The JSON fast path must match the character walk's errors.

Valid input is scanned, parsed, and measured for depth without the walk.
A surrogate, a depth past the limit, ``RecursionError``, or a located
syntax error falls back to that walk, so the message and the caret stay
the same.

A valid ~1 MB document must not run the character walk.

    The walk used to dominate format time. This checks the call, not the clock.

Dotted and bracketed paths over formatted JSON and YAML.

Keys that contain dots, brackets, or non-ASCII characters stay single keys.
Array indexes are zero-based. Missing keys and indexes fail. Formatting twice
does not change the text or the value at a path.

Truncated documents, bad escapes, invalid UTF-8, BOMs, mixed line endings,

column. Invalid UTF-8 names the line and column of the first bad byte.

import multiprocessing

from galley.core.format import format_json
from galley.core.worker import FailureEvent, FormatJob, SuccessEvent, run_worker

def main() -> None:
    # Spawn re-imports this file as __mp_main__. Only the original process
    # checks the start method, and it does so before the child is created.
    assert multiprocessing.get_start_method(allow_none=True) is None
    ctx = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")
    jobs = ctx.Queue()
    events = ctx.Queue()
    process = ctx.Process(target=run_worker, args=(jobs, events))
    assert process._start_method == "spawn"
    process.start()
    text = '{"a": 1}'
    try:
        jobs.put(FormatJob(job_id=1, text=text, source="json", target="json"))
        event = None
        for _ in range(10):
            event = events.get(timeout=30)
            if isinstance(event, (SuccessEvent, FailureEvent)):
                break
        jobs.put(None)
        process.join(timeout=10)
        assert process.exitcode == 0, process.exitcode
        assert isinstance(event, SuccessEvent)
        assert event.text == format_json(text)
        print("ok")
    finally:
        if process.exitcode is None and process.pid is not None:
            process.kill()
            process.join(timeout=5)
        jobs.cancel_join_thread()
        events.cancel_join_thread()
        jobs.close()
        events.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
